title: Piano players Buddy Gurns and Sam Henry in the Gravier Street houses
summary: Gurns was a Gravier Street piano player who taught him sporting house rags; Sam Henry played various houses, including Hattie Rogers's.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Now what about these piano players? Say like Buddy Gurns. Would he have a steady job?

Oh, Buddy Gurns wasn't much. Buddy Gurns, he wasn't much. He was a pretty good piano player. Poor Buddy Gurns. Buddy Gurns, he wasn't much. He was a gravity street player. I don't think he'd ever been down playing no way. Down across Camar Street. Buddy Gurns.
But. What did he teach you?
All rags. All old times. Sporting house rags.
Excuse me. What about someone like Lulu? Was Lulu playing many places?
I got a rag sometime on a piano. And after I played a beautiful thing. Then if I'm around you, I'll tell you the name of it.
I think you told me already. S.H. Rye? Yeah.
So. What would somebody like Sam Henry play?
Would he have a steady job? No.
No, he played around Gravity Street. Just one?
No. Or would he play one house?

He played the first one house and another. Lot of houses. This house, that house. Hattie Rogers. You ever heard of that name Hattie Rogers? On Gravity Street. Hattie Rogers. Have you ever heard of Eloise Blackenstein?
